question.worked_solution:
First, we put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals and then simplify the result:

$$
\sqrt{\frac{9}{64{q}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{9}}{\sqrt{64{q}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{{3}^{2}}}{\sqrt{64{q}^{2}}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{64{q}^{2}}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{64{q}^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{(8q)^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{3}{|8q|} & = \\ \frac{3}{|8|\cdot |q|} & = \\ \frac{3}{8\cdot |q|}\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we are told that $q>0,$ so we have $|q|=q.$ Therefore, the final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8\cdot |q|} & = \\ \frac{3}{8\cdot q} & = \\ \frac{3}{8q}.\end{aligned}
$$
